parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Old Uyghur 𐽰𐽰𐽺𐽳𐽲 (ʾʾnwq /⁠anuḳ⁠/) or Karakhanid اَنُقْ (/⁠anuq⁠/), a derivation from Proto-Turkic *anu- (“to be prepared, made ready”). This word was obsolete in Turkish at least since the 16th Century, but was later reintroduced to replace Arabic-derived hazır.

parole.significato: to put something in vertical position, support
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish دیرهمك (diremek), akin to Old Uyghur [script needed] (tire-, “to support, upright”), from Proto-Turkic *tīre- (“to support”).
Learned borrowing from Old Uyghur 𐾀𐽳𐽶𐽴 (twyz /⁠töz⁠/), from Proto-Turkic *töŕ. Reintroduced to the language during 1940s as a replacement for cevher, a borrowing from Arabic.
